item.text: {"summary":"The failures cluster around negative and boundary time-point decomposition: whole seconds and subseconds appear to be split with truncation toward zero, producing inconsistent calendar fields and negative fractions. The current source excerpts do not show the complete system-time formatter or duration conversion contract needed to confirm the repair site and boundary behavior.","hypotheses":["System-time formatting splits epoch duration into seconds and remainder using truncation toward zero, so negative fractional timestamps produce incorrect calendar and subsecond fields.","Subsecond conversion or signed-to-unsigned formatting mishandles negative remainders, especially at the minimum nanosecond value.","Duration-ratio normalization in the system-time formatter loses carry or borrow when converting nonstandard clock periods."],"queries":["formatter<sys_time<Duration>","duration_cast(std::chrono::duration","write_fractional_seconds","floor< std::chrono::seconds >"],"reads":[{"path":"include/fmt/chrono.h","line":2130,"symbol":"formatter<sys_time<Duration>"},{"path":"include/fmt/chrono.h","line":942,"symbol":"write_fractional_seconds"},{"path":"include/fmt/chrono.h","line":1450,"symbol":"duration_cast"},{"path":"include/fmt/chrono.h","line":810,"symbol":"timestamp_ratios"}],"ready":false}
